primary_meaning: the Holy Spirit (empowering presence that fuels spiritual light, witness, and anointing)
primary_basis: Matthew 25:1-13 (parable of the ten virgins and their lamps)
Zechariah 4:1-14 (lampstand fed by olive oil, identified with the Spirit)
Exodus 27:20-21 and 35:14 (pure oil for the perpetual tabernacle lamp)
1 Samuel 16:13 (anointing oil and the Spirit coming upon David)
Acts 10:38 (Jesus anointed with the Holy Spirit)

alternatives.meaning: spiritual readiness or preparedness for Christ's return
personal faith or saving grace that sustains the believer
good works or deeds of righteousness

notes: Christian tradition overwhelmingly links oil (including lamp oil) with the Holy Spirit as the agent of anointing, empowerment, and sustained spiritual light. The parable of the ten virgins generates secondary debate over readiness, faith, or works, but these remain subordinate to the Spirit association drawn from anointing and Zechariah imagery. No major stream rejects the Spirit symbolism.
